reviewMethod: Antigravity drafts separately reviewed against complete archived version bodies and source notes; source discrepancies retained explicitly.

headings.title: Prohibited practices by performing rights societies
headings.reviewNote: Prohibits performing rights societies and agents from failing to disclose identity/purpose, collecting uncontracted fees, using coercive/retaliatory practices (while permitting Title 17 copyright obligation notices), charging unreasonable royalties, or charging nonprofit musical festivals without providing a requested composition list.

headings.title: Criminal penalty for society violations
headings.reviewNote: Classifies any violation of sections 436.150 to 436.163 as a class C misdemeanor.

entries.reviewSummary: Checked complete archived text (L. 1995 S.B. 355); refined subsection 1 reviewNote to include the federal copyright notice clarification (Title 17) and nonprofit musical festival list prerequisite.

headings.title: Proprietor civil action for injunction and damages
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes a proprietor to bring an action or counterclaim against a performing rights society for an injunction or other legal/equitable relief, and entitles a successful proprietor to actual damages, reasonable attorney's fees, filing fees, and reasonable costs of suit.

headings.title: Cumulative nature of rights and remedies
headings.reviewNote: Establishes that rights, remedies, and prohibitions under sections 436.150 to 436.163 are cumulative to and do not impair common-law, federal, or state statutory rights and remedies.

entries.reviewSummary: Checked complete archived text (L. 1995 S.B. 355); verified counterclaim availability, legal/equitable relief, and cumulative preservation of common-law, federal, and state remedies.

headings.title: Administrative authority of director
headings.reviewNote: Directs the director to administer sections 436.215 to 436.272.

headings.title: Consent to service of process by nonresident agent
headings.reviewNote: Deems engaging in athlete agent business in Missouri by a nonresident individual as appointing the director to accept service of process in related civil actions.

headings.title: Subpoena and document production powers
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes the director to subpoena witnesses and documents, requires service by a person authorized for courts of record, and notes that 'the board' may require sworn copies in lieu of attendance.

headings.title: Circuit court subpoena enforcement
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes the director to seek a show-cause and enforcement order in Cole County, the county of investigation/hearing/proceeding, or any county where the person resides or may be found.

entries.reviewSummary: Checked complete archived text (L. 2004 S.B. 1122); retained all four drafted titles and noted the source text reference to 'the board' for sworn copies in subsection 3.

headings.title: Athlete agent certificate of registration required
headings.reviewNote: Prohibits acting as an athlete agent in Missouri without a certificate of registration under section 436.230 or 436.236, except as provided in subsection 2.

headings.title: Temporary action before registration upon athlete initiation
headings.reviewNote: Permits an individual to act as an athlete agent for all purposes except signing an agency contract if the student athlete or representative initiates communication and the individual applies to register within seven days.

headings.title: Voidness of contracts with unregistered agents
headings.reviewNote: Declares an agency contract resulting from a violation of this section void and requires the athlete agent to return any consideration received under the contract.

entries.reviewSummary: Checked complete archived text (L. 2004 S.B. 1122, A.L. 2021 H.B. 273); refined subsection 2 title to reflect student-athlete-initiated communication and verified return-of-consideration rule in subsection 3.

headings.title: Optional fingerprint submission for licensure applications
headings.reviewNote: Permits the director of the division of professional registration to require fingerprint submissions as part of an athlete agent licensure application.

headings.title: Highway patrol state and federal criminal background check
headings.reviewNote: Requires applicants, when fingerprints are required by the director, to submit them to the Missouri State Highway Patrol for state and federal fingerprint-based criminal history background checks.

headings.title: Central repository, FBI search, and record access
headings.reviewNote: Directs submission of fingerprints and fees to the highway patrol central repository and FBI under section 43.540, requires notification to the director, and grants director access notwithstanding section 610.120.

headings.title: Definition of athlete agent for background checks
headings.reviewNote: Defines 'athlete agent' for purposes of this section, including recruiting, financial/career advising, and business management activities, with an exception for educational-institution employees acting exclusively for the institution.

entries.reviewSummary: Checked complete archived text (L. 2025 S.B. 71 merged with S.B. 81 & 174); replaced all four hallucinated NIL-endorsement draft headings with accurate titles for fingerprint criminal background checks and the section's athlete-agent definition.

headings.title: Application for registration and required disclosures
headings.reviewNote: Requires an individual applicant to submit a prescribed application signed under penalty of perjury containing twenty-one categories of personal, business, disciplinary, litigation, bankruptcy, and league-certification disclosures.

headings.title: Reciprocal registration based on other state certification
headings.reviewNote: Allows an athlete agent registered in another state to apply by submitting the other state's application, a verified statement of material changes (or none) under penalty of perjury, and a copy of the out-of-state certificate.

headings.title: Certificate issuance under reciprocal application
headings.reviewNote: Requires the director to issue a certificate under subsection 2 if the other state's requirements are substantially similar or more restrictive and no revocation, suspension, or pending action exists in any state.

headings.title: Interstate cooperation and information exchange
headings.reviewNote: Directs the director to cooperate with national organizations and other state agencies to develop a common registration form, identify substantially similar states, and exchange agent disciplinary information.

entries.reviewSummary: Checked complete archived text (L. 2004 S.B. 1122, A.L. 2021 H.B. 273); replaced incorrect subsection 4 heading (reciprocal application copy) with director cooperation and information-exchange duties, and removed non-statutory 'Expedited' from subsection 3.

headings.title: Issuance of certificate of registration
headings.reviewNote: Requires the director to issue a certificate of registration to an individual who complies with section 436.227, except as provided in subsection 2.

headings.title: Grounds for refusal to issue registration
headings.reviewNote: Permits the director to refuse registration for conduct significantly adversely affecting fitness, listing seven considerations including occupation-related offenses under section 324.012 and conduct prohibited by section 436.254.

headings.title: Factors in determining applicant fitness
headings.reviewNote: Requires the director, when making a subsection 2 refusal determination, to consider how recently the conduct occurred, its nature and context, and any other relevant conduct of the applicant.

headings.title: Renewal application and continuing eligibility
headings.reviewNote: Permits an athlete agent to apply for renewal on a prescribed form signed under penalty of perjury under section 575.040 with current information on all original registration matters.

headings.title: Reciprocal renewal based on other state certification
headings.reviewNote: Permits an agent registered under section 436.227(3) to renew via subsection 4 or by submitting renewed out-of-state application and registration copies, requiring renewal if standards remain substantially similar and no adverse action is pending.

headings.title: Two-year term of registration certificate
headings.reviewNote: Provides that a certificate of registration or renewal is valid for two years.

entries.reviewSummary: Checked complete archived text (L. 2004 S.B. 1122, A.L. 2020 H.B. 2046, A.L. 2021 H.B. 273); corrected subsection 3 reviewNote to match the three statutory fitness considerations (recency, nature/context, and other relevant conduct).

headings.title: Grounds for suspension, revocation, or refusal to renew
headings.reviewNote: Permits the director to revoke, suspend, or refuse to renew a registration for subsection 2 causes and requires written notice of refusal reasons and the right to file a chapter 621 complaint with the administrative hearing commission.

headings.title: Director complaint to commission and disciplinary causes
headings.reviewNote: Permits the director to file a chapter 621 complaint with the administrative hearing commission against current, unrenewed, or surrendered registrants for nine enumerated causes including crimes, fraud, misconduct, drug violations, and deceptive solicitation.

headings.title: Hearing commission proceedings and disciplinary sanctions
headings.reviewNote: Directs chapter 621 proceedings and authorizes the director, upon a commission finding of grounds, to warn, censure, impose probation up to six months, suspend up to one year, restrict indefinitely, or revoke registration.

headings.title: Reinstatement waiting period after revocation
headings.reviewNote: Permits a revocation order to bar reapplication for reinstatement for two to seven years from the order date, with all stay orders tolling that period.

entries.reviewSummary: Checked complete archived text (L. 2004 S.B. 1122); replaced shifted/incorrect draft headings for subsections 2, 3, and 4 (AHC complaint causes, disciplinary sanctions, and two-to-seven-year reinstatement bar).

headings.title: Registration fees and athlete agent fund creation
headings.reviewNote: Requires rule-set registration and renewal fees deposited into the Athlete Agent Fund and overrides section 33.080 biennial general-revenue sweeps below two- or three-times prior-year appropriations (no sweep before August 28, 2006).

headings.title: Document rulemaking and chapter 536 nonseverability
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes the director to promulgate rules to authorize and file athlete agent documents under section 536.010, subject to chapter 536 and section 536.028 compliance and post-August 28, 2003 nonseverability invalidation.

entries.reviewSummary: Checked complete archived text (L. 2004 S.B. 1122); replaced incorrect subsection 1 heading (drafted as rulemaking) with application/renewal fees and Athlete Agent Fund creation/sweep rules, and updated subsection 2 to include document rulemaking.

headings.title: Mandatory writing and signature requirements for agency contract
headings.reviewNote: Requires an agency contract to be in a record signed by the parties.

headings.title: Required contractual disclosures and fee terms
headings.reviewNote: Requires an agency contract to state registration status, compensation calculation, unlisted compensated persons, reimbursable expenses, services, duration, and execution date.

headings.title: Prominent boldface warning to student athlete
headings.reviewNote: Requires a conspicuous boldface all-caps warning table near the student athlete's signature covering eligibility loss, 72-hour athletic-director notice, and 14-day cancellation.

headings.title: Separate signed acknowledgment of eligibility risk
headings.reviewNote: Requires a separate record signed by the student athlete (or parent/guardian of a minor) acknowledging that signing the contract may cause loss of athletic eligibility.

headings.title: Voidability of nonconforming contract and no refund duty
headings.reviewNote: Makes a nonconforming agency contract voidable by the student athlete (or parent/guardian of a minor) without requiring return of inducement consideration received from the agent.

headings.title: Delivery of executed contract copy to student athlete
headings.reviewNote: Requires the athlete agent to give a copy of the signed agency contract to the student athlete or, for a minor, to the parent or guardian.

headings.title: Parent or guardian signature for minor student athlete
headings.reviewNote: Requires a minor student athlete's agency contract to be signed by the parent or guardian and requires corresponding revision of the subsection 3 warning notice.

entries.reviewSummary: Checked complete archived text including the embedded boldface warning table (L. 2004 S.B. 1122, A.L. 2021 H.B. 273); corrected shifted draft headings in subsections 4, 5, and 7.

headings.title: Definition of communicating or attempting to communicate
headings.reviewNote: Defines 'communicating or attempting to communicate' for this section as contacting or attempting to contact by in-person meeting, record, or any other message-conveying method.

headings.title: Agent notice to athletic director of agency contract
headings.reviewNote: Requires the athlete agent to notify the athletic director in a record within seventy-two hours of entering an agency contract or before the next scheduled athletic event, whichever occurs first.

headings.title: Notice to subsequent educational institution upon enrollment
headings.reviewNote: Requires an athlete agent to notify the athletic director within seventy-two hours after the agent knows or should have known a contracted student athlete subsequently enrolled.

headings.title: Agent notice of pre-enrollment relationship with scholarship athlete
headings.reviewNote: Requires an athlete agent to notify the athletic director within ten days after enrollment of a pre-enrollment recruiting/solicitation relationship with an athletic-scholarship student athlete.

headings.title: Prior agent notice before initiating recruiting communication
headings.reviewNote: Requires an athlete agent to give notice in a record to the athletic director before communicating or attempting to communicate to influence an enrolled student athlete, minor's parent/guardian, or intermediary.

headings.title: Agent notice upon athlete-initiated communication
headings.reviewNote: Requires an athlete agent to notify the athletic director in a record within ten days after communication or attempted communication initiated by or on behalf of an enrolled student athlete.

headings.title: Educational institution duty to report agent violations
headings.reviewNote: Requires an educational institution aware of an athlete agent's violation of sections 436.215 to 436.272 to notify the director and any known licensing professional league or players' association.

headings.title: Student athlete duty to inform athletic director
headings.reviewNote: Requires the student athlete to inform the athletic director in a record within seventy-two hours of entering an agency contract or before the next athletic event, including the agent's name and contact information.

entries.reviewSummary: Checked complete archived text (L. 2004 S.B. 1122, A.L. 2021 H.B. 273); corrected shifted draft headings in subsections 1, 2, 4, and 5 (definition, 72-hour contract notice, 10-day scholarship-relationship notice, and prior notice before agent-initiated contact).

headings.title: Student athlete right to cancel agency contract
headings.reviewNote: Permits a student athlete, or parent or guardian of a minor, to cancel an agency contract by written notice to the athlete agent within fourteen days after signing.

headings.title: Nonwaiver of cancellation right
headings.reviewNote: Prohibits a student athlete, or parent or guardian of a minor, from waiving the right to cancel an agency contract.

headings.title: No liability or return of consideration upon cancellation
headings.reviewNote: Relieves a student athlete, parent, or guardian who cancels within fourteen days from paying contract consideration or returning inducement consideration received from the agent.

entries.reviewSummary: Checked complete archived text (L. 2004 S.B. 1122, A.L. 2021 H.B. 273); retained all three drafted titles and verified fourteen-day written cancellation, nonwaiver, and no consideration/inducement return.

headings.title: Mandatory five-year record retention by athlete agent
headings.reviewNote: Requires an athlete agent to retain client names and addresses, agency contracts, and direct recruitment or solicitation costs for five years.

headings.title: Records open to inspection by director
headings.reviewNote: Makes records required under subsection 1 open to inspection by the director during normal business hours.

entries.reviewSummary: Checked complete archived text (L. 2004 S.B. 1122); retained both drafted titles and verified five-year retention scope and normal-business-hours director inspection.

headings.title: Civil cause of action for institution or student athlete
headings.reviewNote: Permits an educational institution or student athlete adversely affected by an agent's violation of sections 436.215 to 436.272 to sue for damages, defining adverse effect by suspension/disqualification or financial damage.

headings.title: Damages, attorney fees, and forfeiture of compensation
headings.reviewNote: Permits a prevailing plaintiff to recover actual damages, costs, and reasonable attorney's fees, and requires a liable agent to forfeit payment rights and refund consideration paid.

headings.title: Classification as unfair trade practice
headings.reviewNote: Deems any violation of sections 436.215 to 436.272 an unfair trade practice for purposes of sections 375.930 to 375.948.

entries.reviewSummary: Checked complete archived text (L. 2004 S.B. 1122, A.L. 2021 H.B. 273); retained all three drafted titles and verified adverse-effect qualification criteria and section 375.930 to 375.948 unfair trade practice cross-reference.

headings.title: Criminal misdemeanor penalty and civil fine
headings.reviewNote: Makes any individual violating sections 436.215 to 436.272 guilty of a class A misdemeanor and liable for a civil penalty up to $100,000.

headings.title: Knowing violation as class E felony
headings.reviewNote: Makes any individual knowingly violating sections 436.215 to 436.272 guilty of a class E felony and liable for a civil penalty up to $100,000.

entries.reviewSummary: Checked complete archived text (L. 2004 S.B. 1122, A.L. 2021 H.B. 273); retained both drafted titles and verified class A misdemeanor, class E felony for knowing violations, and $100,000 civil penalty cap.

headings.title: Tender of substitute security for retainage release
headings.reviewNote: Permits a non-defaulting contractor to tender acceptable section 436.312 substitute security with a written request for cash release or non-withholding of retainage.

headings.title: Owner duty to pay or refrain from withholding retainage
headings.reviewNote: Requires the owner to pay withheld retainage within five working days after tender or, if tendered before withholding, refrain from withholding retainage from future payments.

entries.reviewSummary: Checked complete archived text (L. 2002 H.B. 1403); retained both drafted titles and verified non-default condition and five-working-day payment deadline.

headings.title: Acceptable forms of substitute security for retainage
headings.reviewNote: Lists acceptable substitute security for sections 436.306 and 436.309: Missouri bank certificates of deposit, surety retainage bonds, and irrevocable unconditional letters of credit (with a 60-day letter-of-credit nonrenewal draw rule placed in subdivision (1)).

headings.title: Contractor entitlement to earned interest and income
headings.reviewNote: Entitles the contractor in all events to all interest and income earned on securities deposited in substitution for retainage.

entries.reviewSummary: Checked complete archived text (L. 2002 H.B. 1403); retained both drafted titles and noted the source-text placement of the 60-day letter-of-credit renewal/draw rule inside subdivision (1).

headings.title: Contractor notice of right to cure construction defects
headings.reviewNote: Requires a contractor to provide conspicuous notice at contract entry (or in a condominium public offering statement) of the right to offer to cure construction defects under sections 436.350 to 436.365.

headings.title: Statutory disclosure form and time frame guidelines
headings.reviewNote: Requires the notice to include time frame guidelines and sets out the mandatory all-caps disclosure text referencing the small-claims exception and section 436.356(10) emergency repairs.

headings.title: Failure to give notice bars procedural defense
headings.reviewNote: Provides that sections 436.350 to 436.365 do not bar an action or apply to a claimant's claim if the contractor failed to provide the required written notice.

headings.title: Exemption for counterclaims in contractor-initiated lawsuits
headings.reviewNote: Exempts homeowner or association construction-defect counterclaims and affirmative defenses in lawsuits originally filed by a contractor, while requiring compliance for uncovered claims.

entries.reviewSummary: Checked complete archived text (L. 2005 S.B. 168 § 431.303); replaced incorrect subsection 4 heading (drafted as new construction/remodel scope) with the exemption for homeowner counterclaims and affirmative defenses in contractor-initiated lawsuits.

headings.title: Written claim of defect as condition precedent to action
headings.reviewNote: Requires a claimant in an action arising from residential construction or substantial remodel to serve the contractor a written notice of claim describing the defect and known results in reasonable detail.

headings.title: Contractor response time and election of remedies
headings.reviewNote: Requires the contractor within fourteen days of service to serve a written response proposing inspection, offering repair and/or monetary settlement (including residence purchase), or disputing the claim.

headings.title: Claimant suit, rejection, mediation, and access for repairs
headings.reviewNote: Permits immediate suit upon dispute or nonresponse; governs written rejection, mediation under section 436.362, and 30-day offer termination; and requires reasonable access for accepted non-inspection repair offers.

headings.title: Inspection procedures, post-inspection offer, and rejection
headings.reviewNote: Requires inspection scheduling within fourteen days at contractor cost (repairing destructive testing damage), a fourteen-day post-inspection report and offer/denial, and governs non-compliance suits, rejection, mediation, and 30-day termination.

headings.title: Acceptance of post-inspection repair offer and modification
headings.reviewNote: Requires written acceptance within thirty days of a subsection 4(2)(a) or (b) repair offer, grants reasonable access, allows mediation of performance disputes, and permits mutual written modification of scope or timetable.

headings.title: Dismissal without prejudice for premature court action
headings.reviewNote: Subjects an action commenced before complying with this section to dismissal without prejudice upon motion if the court finds the claimant knowingly violated the act.

headings.title: Amended claim notice for later-discovered defects
headings.reviewNote: Permits amending a notice of claim for later-discovered defects upon compliance with this section, and allows adding defects discovered after suit commencement only after notice and subsection 2 response opportunity.

headings.title: Filing and abatement to preserve expiring limitations
headings.reviewNote: Permits filing an action if a limitations period would expire during the pre-suit process, with immediate abatement pending completion, without reviving expired limitations or extending statutes of repose.

headings.title: Inadmissibility of claim notice and contractor response
headings.reviewNote: Treats written notices of claim and contractor responses as settlement offers inadmissible in related defect actions (except as permitted by law) and bars their use as prior inconsistent statements.

headings.title: Emergency repairs exception to pre-suit procedure
headings.reviewNote: Permits immediate reasonable repairs for defects (including defective garage doors) threatening life/safety or significant additional residence damage and inclusion of their cost in the claim, while excluding non-emergency homeowner repairs.

headings.title: Location of construction defect mediation
headings.reviewNote: Requires any mediation to take place in the county where the claimant resides or in a mutually agreed location.

entries.reviewSummary: Checked complete archived text (L. 2005 S.B. 168 § 431.306); corrected non-statutory 90-day claim in subsection 1 reviewNote and replaced shifted/incorrect draft headings across subsections 3, 5, 6, 7, 8, 9, and 11.

headings.title: Applicability after association board rejects settlement offer
headings.reviewNote: Applies this section before an association files a common-area defect suit when the governing board rejects a contractor's written settlement offer that included a written request for a member meeting.

headings.title: Open association member meeting before filing action
headings.reviewNote: Requires the association board to hold a meeting open to each member at least fifteen days before commencing an action against the contractor.

headings.title: Advance written meeting notice and required disclosures
headings.reviewNote: Requires written notice to each member at least fifteen days before the meeting stating meeting details, available options and funding/assessment impacts, and the contractor's complete final settlement offer and reasons.

headings.title: Evidentiary privilege for meeting discussions and notice
headings.reviewNote: Deems meeting discussions and required notice contents privileged communications inadmissible in any action unless the association consents.

headings.title: Single contractor request limit for member meeting
headings.reviewNote: Limits a contractor to no more than one request to meet and discuss a written settlement offer under this section.

entries.reviewSummary: Checked complete archived text (L. 2005 S.B. 168 § 431.309); replaced all five hallucinated tolling/repose draft headings with accurate headings for association member-meeting requirements after settlement-offer rejection.

headings.title: Nonbinding mediation request, response, and cost sharing
headings.reviewNote: Allows either party to offer nonbinding independent mediation at any time with equally shared neutral mediator costs, a 14-day written response deadline, and mediation within 45 days of request.

headings.title: Optional inclusion of reasonably necessary third parties
headings.reviewNote: Permits either party to include persons or entities reasonably necessary to resolve the claim without mandating attendance by anyone other than the contractor or noticed claimant.

headings.title: Subpoena immunity for arbitrators, conciliators, and mediators
headings.reviewNote: Bars subpoenaing or compelling any agreed arbitrator, conciliator, mediator, or their agent/employee to disclose matters disclosed in setting up or conducting the proceeding.

headings.title: Settlement negotiation status and Rule 17 confidentiality
headings.reviewNote: Treats arbitration, conciliation, and mediation proceedings as settlement negotiations subject to confidentiality under Missouri Supreme Court Rule 17.

headings.title: Scope and timing of claim release after resolution
headings.reviewNote: Provides that resolution releases only the claim described in the notice of defect and does not take effect until the agreed-upon remedy has been accomplished.

entries.reviewSummary: Checked complete archived text (L. 2005 S.B. 168 § 431.312); replaced all five hallucinated draft headings with accurate mediation, third-party participation, privilege, confidentiality, and limited-release headings.

headings.title: Preservation of remedies, contracts, and access rights
headings.reviewNote: Clarifies that sections 436.350 to 436.365 create no new liability theory, do not limit existing remedies or employment/contractual relationships, and do not restrict existing access or inspection rights.

headings.title: Binding arbitration contracts under chapter 435
headings.reviewNote: Allows contractor-homeowner contracts to specify binding arbitration under chapter 435, exempting such contracts from sections 436.350 to 436.365 when the contractor provides section 435.460 notice.

headings.title: Exemption for insurer subrogation actions
headings.reviewNote: Exempts actions brought by an insurer subrogated to a claimant's rights following payment under an insurance policy.

entries.reviewSummary: Checked complete archived text (L. 2005 S.B. 168 § 431.315); replaced all three hallucinated draft headings with accurate headings for preserved remedies/relationships, chapter 435 binding arbitration, and insurer subrogation exclusion.

headings.title: Definitions for preneed funeral contract statutes
headings.reviewNote: Defines twelve statutory terms (including beneficiary, board, guaranteed/nonguaranteed contract, insurance-/joint account-/trust-funded preneed contract, market value, preneed contract, preneed trust, purchaser, and trustee) for sections 436.400 to 436.520.

headings.title: Incorporation of chapter 333 definitions
headings.reviewNote: Deems all terms defined in chapter 333 to carry the same meaning when used in sections 436.400 to 436.520.

entries.reviewSummary: Checked complete archived text (L. 2009 S.B. 1, A.L. 2011 H.B. 265 merged with S.B. 325); replaced both hallucinated seller-licensing draft headings with accurate headings for preneed definitions and chapter 333 incorporation.

headings.title: Provider obligation to furnish preneed services and goods
headings.reviewNote: Obligates the provider designated in a preneed contract, except as otherwise provided in sections 436.400 to 436.520, to furnish the described disposition, funeral or burial services and facilities, and merchandise.

headings.title: Seller obligation to collect, deposit, and disburse payments
headings.reviewNote: Obligates the designated seller to collect and properly deposit and disburse all purchaser payments and ensure statutory and contractual duties are met in compliance with sections 436.400 to 436.520.

entries.reviewSummary: Checked complete archived text (L. 2009 S.B. 1); replaced both hallucinated provider-licensing draft headings with accurate headings for provider service obligations and seller payment/compliance duties.

headings.title: Written agreement required between seller and provider
headings.reviewNote: Prohibits designating a provider in a preneed contract without a written contractual agreement with the seller, except when seller and provider are the same legal entity.

headings.title: Required contents of provider-seller written agreement
headings.reviewNote: Requires the written agreement to include provider consent, payment tracking and remittance procedures with authorized timeframes, and dated signatures of seller and provider (original-rolls footnote: 'signature was').

headings.title: Provider notification to board within fifteen days
headings.reviewNote: Requires a provider to notify the board within fifteen days of authorizing or agreeing to allow a seller to designate it as provider under any preneed contract.

headings.title: Duty to furnish contract copies upon board request
headings.reviewNote: Requires a seller, provider, or preneed agent, upon board request, to provide the board a copy of any preneed contract or seller-provider agreement.

entries.reviewSummary: Checked complete archived text and original-rolls footnote ('signature was') (L. 2009 S.B. 1); replaced all four hallucinated preneed-sale draft headings with accurate provider-seller written agreement headings.

headings.title: Mandatory preneed contract form and disclosures
headings.reviewNote: Requires sequentially numbered, readable written preneed contracts containing sixteen conspicuous elements covering parties, licenses, services, funding type, insurance/transfer/cancellation notices, revocability, guarantees, installment death disclosures, and signatures.

headings.title: Voidability of noncompliant or unauthorized preneed contracts
headings.reviewNote: Makes a preneed contract voidable by the purchaser or legal representative upon court determination of noncompliance, unlicensed seller under chapter 333, or non-consenting provider, with full payment recovery.

headings.title: Irrevocable benefit waiver for public assistance eligibility
headings.reviewNote: Permits a beneficiary seeking public assistance under chapter 208 or other state/federal law to execute and deliver an irrevocable written waiver of refund or payment rights.

headings.title: Purchaser right to cancel, rescind, or transfer contract
headings.reviewNote: Affirms purchasers' statutory rights under this chapter to cancel or rescind a revocable preneed contract and transfer any preneed contract with or without cause.

headings.title: Written purchaser consent to change funding method
headings.reviewNote: Prohibits changing a preneed contract among trust-funded, insurance-funded, and joint account-funded types without the purchaser's written consent.

entries.reviewSummary: Checked complete archived text (L. 2009 S.B. 1); replaced all five hallucinated trust-deposit draft headings with accurate preneed contract form, voidability, public-assistance waiver, cancellation/transfer, and funding-change headings.

headings.title: Compliance standard for trust-funded guaranteed contracts
headings.reviewNote: Requires trust-funded guaranteed preneed contracts to comply with sections 436.400 to 436.520 and this section.

headings.title: Sixty-day trust deposit deadline and fee restriction
headings.reviewNote: Requires sellers to deposit all payments into the designated preneed trust within sixty days of receipt and prohibits unauthorized consumer fees beyond chapter 333, this chapter, or other state/federal law.

headings.title: Five percent origination fee distribution to seller
headings.reviewNote: Permits a seller to request distribution of up to the first five percent of total contract amount as an origination fee once five percent is deposited, payable by the trustee within fifteen days.

headings.title: Additional ten percent face-value distribution to seller
headings.reviewNote: Permits the trustee, upon written seller request after consumer payment deposit, to distribute up to an additional ten percent of contract face value within fifteen days or per written agreement.

headings.title: Qualified financial institution trustee for preneed trust
headings.reviewNote: Requires the preneed trustee to be a state- or federally-chartered financial institution authorized to exercise trust powers in Missouri and to hold deposits as trust principal.

headings.title: Trustee independence and control presumption
headings.reviewNote: Prohibits common control between the trustee institution and the seller or preneed agent, presuming control at ten percent voting-security ownership unless rebutted before the board.

headings.title: Commingling of contract funds with individual accounting
headings.reviewNote: Permits commingling payments from multiple preneed contracts in one trust if the trustee maintains records separately identifying each contract's payments, earnings, and distributions.

headings.title: Trustee portfolio review upon accepting trust assets
headings.reviewNote: Requires a trustee within a reasonable time after accepting trusteeship or assets to review and adjust holdings to comply with trust purposes, terms, and sections 436.400 to 436.520.

headings.title: Payment of trust administrative expenses from income
headings.reviewNote: Permits paying trust establishment and administration expenses from investment income only, barring use of principal and allocating shortfalls per written agreements among seller, provider, and trustee.

headings.title: Accrual and distribution of trust income upon performance
headings.reviewNote: Allocates trust investment income to seller and provider per contract, requires accrual until final disposition and service delivery (unless cancelled), and applies to trusts established on or after August 28, 2009.

headings.title: Certificate of performance and seller payment to provider
headings.reviewNote: Requires providers to submit a jointly signed certificate of performance, entitles providers without a written contract to allocable trust asset market value (original-rolls footnote: 'trusts'), and requires seller payment within sixty days.

headings.title: Provider direct demand on trustee for unpaid amounts
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes a provider, if a seller fails to make timely payment, to demand direct distribution from the preneed trustee of all amounts the seller would be entitled to receive for the contract.

headings.title: Trustee recordkeeping, annual reporting, and purchaser statements
headings.reviewNote: Requires trustees (including pre-August 28, 2009 trusts) to maintain transaction records and assist with section 436.460 annual reports, and requires sellers to furnish deposit statements within thirty days of written purchaser request.

headings.title: Termination of preneed trust and final distribution
headings.reviewNote: Terminates a preneed trust (including pre-August 28, 2009 trusts) when trust principal holds no preneed contract payments, requiring distribution of all remaining principal and undistributed income to the establishing seller.

entries.reviewSummary: Checked complete archived text and original-rolls footnote ('trusts' in subsection 11) (L. 2009 S.B. 1); replaced all fourteen shifted/hallucinated draft headings with exact subsection-by-subsection headings for trust-funded guaranteed preneed contracts.

headings.title: Compliance deadline for pre-existing preneed trusts
headings.reviewNote: Requires preneed trusts existing on August 28, 2009, to comply with applicable provisions taking effect that date no later than July 1, 2010.

headings.title: Growth investment mandate and term life insurance ban
headings.reviewNote: Requires trustees to invest trust property only in investments with reasonable potential for growth or income and prohibits investing trust funds in any term life insurance product.

headings.title: Prudent investor standard and use of special skills
headings.reviewNote: Requires trustees to invest and manage trust assets as a prudent investor with reasonable care, skill, and caution, and to apply any special skills or expertise possessed or represented.

headings.title: Duty to diversify preneed trust investments
headings.reviewNote: Requires trustees to diversify trust investments unless special circumstances reasonably make the trust's purpose better served without diversification.

headings.title: Investment factors in prudent management
headings.reviewNote: Lists six factors a trustee must consider when relevant: economic conditions, inflation/deflation, tax consequences, portfolio role, expected total return, and liquidity/income/capital preservation needs.

headings.title: Prohibition against borrowing against preneed trust assets
headings.reviewNote: Bars sellers, providers, and agents from taking loans against trust assets and, as of August 29, 2009, prohibits pledging existing preneed contracts as loan collateral or taking unauthorized loans of preneed funds.

entries.reviewSummary: Checked complete archived text (L. 2009 S.B. 1); replaced shifted draft headings in subsections 1 through 4 (July 1, 2010 compliance deadline, growth/income investment and term-life ban, prudent investor standard, and diversification).

headings.title: Application to all preneed trusts regardless of creation date
headings.reviewNote: Applies this section to all preneed trusts, including trusts established before August 28, 2009.

headings.title: Prudent delegation of trustee duties and powers
headings.reviewNote: Permits a preneed trustee to delegate duties and powers prudently, requiring reasonable care, skill, and caution in selecting agents, setting agency scope/terms, and periodically monitoring performance.

headings.title: Agent duty of reasonable care to preneed trust
headings.reviewNote: Imposes a duty on an agent performing a delegated function to exercise reasonable care to comply with the agency terms.

headings.title: Agent submission to state court jurisdiction
headings.reviewNote: Provides that accepting delegated powers or duties from a preneed trustee submits the agent to Missouri court jurisdiction.

headings.title: Non-exoneration of preneed trustee for delegated acts
headings.reviewNote: Provides that delegating duties or powers to an agent does not relieve the trustee of duties or responsibilities under sections 436.400 to 436.520 or the trust agreement.

headings.title: Grandfathered independent financial advisors
headings.reviewNote: Permits trusts in existence as of August 28, 2009, to continue using an independent financial advisor who was in place under section 436.031 on that date.

entries.reviewSummary: Checked complete archived text (L. 2009 S.B. 1); retained all six drafted titles and verified grandfathered section 436.031 independent financial advisor provision in subsection 6.

headings.title: Insurance-funded preneed contract compliance standards
headings.reviewNote: Requires insurance-funded preneed contracts to comply with sections 436.400 to 436.520 and this section.

headings.title: Fee restrictions and loan collateral prohibition
headings.reviewNote: Bars collecting amounts beyond insurer-assessed premiums or authorized charges and, as of August 29, 2009, bars using existing preneed contracts as loan collateral or taking unauthorized loans of preneed funds.

headings.title: Thirty-day remittance deadline to insurance carrier
headings.reviewNote: Requires prompt remittance of collected payments to the insurer or designee and prohibits holding payments for more than thirty days from receipt.

headings.title: Prohibition against borrowing against preneed insurance policies
headings.reviewNote: Makes it unlawful for a seller, provider, or preneed agent to procure or accept a loan against an insurance contract funding a preneed contract.

headings.title: Interplay with general state insurance laws
headings.reviewNote: Provides that insurance laws do not apply to preneed contracts but do apply to accompanying insurance/annuities, while exempting annuities and policies regulated under chapters 374, 375, and 376 from sections 436.400 to 436.520.

headings.title: Application to all preneed contracts regardless of date
headings.reviewNote: Applies this section to all preneed contracts, including those entered into before August 28, 2009.

headings.title: Policy ownership and beneficiary designation rules
headings.reviewNote: Requires for post-August 28, 2009 insurance-funded contracts that the purchaser or beneficiary own the policy and that the seller or provider be named beneficiary or assignee for validity and enforceability.

headings.title: Disposition of life insurance policy proceeds overage
headings.reviewNote: Directs any life insurance proceeds exceeding actual goods and services costs on a nonguaranteed preneed contract to the beneficiary's estate or, if the beneficiary received public assistance, to the state of Missouri.

entries.reviewSummary: Checked complete archived text (L. 2009 S.B. 1, A.L. 2011 H.B. 265 merged with S.B. 325); retained all eight drafted titles and verified August 28/29, 2009 dates and chapters 374, 375, and 376 interplay.

headings.title: Joint account-funded preneed contract standards
headings.reviewNote: Requires joint account-funded preneed contracts to comply with sections 436.400 to 436.520 and this section.

headings.title: Separate joint account or pay-on-death account authorization
headings.reviewNote: Permits written agreement to deposit funds into a separate joint or beneficiary pay-on-death account at a Missouri-authorized financial institution, with withdrawals limited to dual signatures, pay-on-death, or reasonable administrative expenses.

headings.title: Ten-day deposit deadline into joint account
headings.reviewNote: Requires all consideration paid under a joint account-funded contract to be deposited into an authorized joint account within ten days of seller receipt.

headings.title: Permitted investments and exclusion of term life insurance
headings.reviewNote: Directs the financial institution to hold and invest funds in depositor accounts per written agreement while barring term life insurance or investments lacking reasonable potential for income or appreciation.

headings.title: Application of interest and administrative expenses
headings.reviewNote: Directs account income to pay reasonable financial-institution administration expenses with the balance distributed or reinvested upon fulfillment, cancellation, or transfer.

headings.title: Disbursement of joint account funds upon contract fulfillment
headings.reviewNote: Requires the seller within fifteen days of receiving a jointly signed certificate of performance to take institution steps to secure funds and pay the provider within ten days of receiving the funds.

headings.title: Prohibition against borrowing against joint account funds
headings.reviewNote: Bars sellers, providers, and preneed agents from borrowing against joint account assets and, as of August 28, 2009, prohibits pledging preneed contracts as loan collateral or taking unauthorized loans.

entries.reviewSummary: Checked complete archived text (L. 2009 S.B. 1, A.L. 2011 H.B. 265 merged with S.B. 325); retained all seven drafted titles and verified fifteen-day/ten-day disbursement timelines and August 28, 2009 loan-collateral ban.

headings.title: Seller right to cancel contract for installment default
headings.reviewNote: Grants a seller the right to cancel a trust-funded or joint-account-funded preneed contract if the purchaser defaults on an installment payment for over sixty days.

headings.title: Thirty-day written notice of default and cancellation date
headings.reviewNote: Requires written notice to the purchaser and provider before cancellation stating the amount due, due date, and cancellation date if payment is not received within thirty days of postmark.

headings.title: Seller election to convert to nonguaranteed contract
headings.reviewNote: Permits the seller, if payment is not remitted within thirty days of postmark, either to cancel the contract or continue it as a nonguaranteed contract crediting all trust payments made.

headings.title: Eighty-five percent refund to purchaser upon cancellation
headings.reviewNote: Requires refunding eighty-five percent of contract payments to the purchaser upon seller cancellation under this section, with all remaining funds distributed to the seller.

entries.reviewSummary: Checked complete archived text (L. 2009 S.B. 1); retained all four drafted titles and verified 60-day default, 30-day postmarked notice, nonguaranteed conversion option, and 85% purchaser refund.

headings.title: Purchaser right to designate alternative preneed provider
headings.reviewNote: Permits a purchaser to designate a consenting alternative provider by written notice to the seller and original provider without penalty or additional transfer fee.

headings.title: Seller duty to remit funds to alternative provider
headings.reviewNote: Requires the seller to pay the newly designated provider all amounts owed to the original provider, transfers provider obligations to the new provider, and keeps interest allocated to the seller per contract.

headings.title: Trust continuation or transfer for trust-funded contracts
headings.reviewNote: Requires a seller, upon written notice of an alternative provider for a trust-funded contract, either to continue the trust with the new provider or pay all trust principal and income to the new trust.

entries.reviewSummary: Checked complete archived text (L. 2009 S.B. 1); replaced incorrect subsection 3 heading (drafted as original provider relief) with trust continuation or transfer options for trust-funded contracts.

headings.title: Annual reporting requirement for preneed sellers
headings.reviewNote: Requires each seller to file an annual report under oath with eleven required disclosures including contracts sold/fulfilled/cancelled/transferred, agents, providers, record custodian, and audit consents (original-rolls footnote: 'preened').

headings.title: Additional annual report disclosures for trust-funded contracts
headings.reviewNote: Requires sellers of trust-funded contracts to report depository/account numbers, balances, contributions, earnings, distributions, expenses, and trustee corporate-officer certification under oath (original-rolls footnote: 'section 1').

headings.title: Additional annual report disclosures for joint account contracts
headings.reviewNote: Requires sellers of joint account-funded contracts to report Missouri depository/account numbers, deposits, balances, contributions, earnings, distributions, expenses, and financial-institution certification under oath.

headings.title: Additional annual report disclosures for insurance-funded contracts
headings.reviewNote: Requires sellers of insurance-funded contracts to report insurers, policy status and face value, funds received and forwarding dates, and insurer representative certification under oath.

headings.title: Annual reporting fee per preneed contract sold
headings.reviewNote: Requires each seller to remit a rule-set annual reporting fee for each preneed contract sold since the last report, collectible from the purchaser or paid from seller funds.

headings.title: October 31 filing deadline and late fee
headings.reviewNote: Requires filing annual reports by October 31 each year (or rule-established date) and subjects late filings to a rule-established late fee.

headings.title: Automatic license suspension for delinquent annual report
headings.reviewNote: Automatically suspends a seller's preneed seller license for failure to file the annual report on or before its due date until the report is filed and applicable fees are paid.

headings.title: Application to preneed contracts entered before August 28, 2009
headings.reviewNote: Provides that this section applies to preneed contracts entered into before August 28, 2009.

entries.reviewSummary: Checked complete archived text and original-rolls footnotes ('preened' in sub 1(1), 'section 1' in sub 2) (L. 2009 S.B. 1); replaced all seven shifted/incorrect draft headings in subsections 2 through 8.

headings.title: Public complaints and mandatory board investigation
headings.reviewNote: Allows any person to file a complaint with the board alleging a violation of this chapter and requires the board to investigate each complaint.

headings.title: Board inspections, investigations, and five-year financial exams
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes board inspections, investigations, and financial examinations of providers, sellers, agents, trusts, and joint accounts with or without cause, requiring seller financial exams at least every five years subject to funding.

headings.title: Board authorization notice defining examination scope
headings.reviewNote: Requires the board, upon deciding to conduct an inspection, investigation, examination, or audit, to issue a notice authorizing an appointed person and instructing its scope.

headings.title: Conflict-of-interest bar for appointed examiners
headings.reviewNote: Prohibits appointing any person with a conflict of interest, management affiliation, or pecuniary interest in a regulated entity to conduct an inspection, investigation, examination, or audit.

headings.title: Interagency investigative and examination assistance
headings.reviewNote: Permits the board to request investigators or financial examiners from the division of professional registration, department of commerce and insurance, or attorney general, which shall not be unreasonably withheld.

headings.title: Right of entry onto preneed business premises
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes the person conducting an inspection, investigation, or audit to enter business offices, premises, or establishments where preneed funerals are sold, provided, or advertised.

headings.title: Licensee and registrant duty to produce records
headings.reviewNote: Requires licensees and registrants upon board request to make books and records available for inspection and copying at reasonable times, including insurance, trust, joint account, and financial institution records.

headings.title: Board subpoena power for records and papers
headings.reviewNote: Empowers the board to issue subpoenas compelling production of records and papers by licensees, trustees, or registrants, served in the same manner as criminal subpoenas.

headings.title: Mandatory cooperation with regulatory agencies
headings.reviewNote: Requires sellers, providers, preneed agents, and trustees to cooperate with the board, division of finance, department of commerce and insurance, and attorney general in inspections, investigations, examinations, or audits.

headings.title: Board authority to file broader hearing commission complaints
headings.reviewNote: Clarifies that this section does not limit the board's authority to file administrative hearing commission complaints regardless of whether charges exceed or lack a preliminary public complaint.

headings.title: Interagency sharing of preneed investigation information
headings.reviewNote: Permits the board, division of finance, department of commerce and insurance, and attorney general to share information relating to preneed inspections, investigations, examinations, or audits.

headings.title: Attorney general judicial actions for preneed violations
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes the attorney general, when an inspection, investigation, examination, or audit reveals a violation of sections 436.400 to 436.520, to initiate judicial proceedings for fourteen categories of legal and trust relief.

entries.reviewSummary: Checked complete archived text (L. 2009 S.B. 1); replaced all twelve hallucinated provider-annual-report draft headings with accurate complaint, inspection, financial-examination, subpoena, interagency, and attorney-general judicial-action headings.

headings.title: Class D felony penalty and concurrent prosecution
headings.reviewNote: Makes knowing and willful violations of sections 436.400 to 436.520 by incompetence, misconduct, gross negligence, fraud, misrepresentation, or dishonesty a class D felony (each violation separate), granting the attorney general concurrent prosecutorial jurisdiction.

headings.title: Merchandising practices violation and license revocation
headings.reviewNote: Deems any violation of sections 436.400 to 436.520 a violation of section 407.020, authorizing chapter 407 relief/penalties and court-ordered license or registration revocation or suspension in attorney general proceedings.

entries.reviewSummary: Checked complete archived text and effective date (1-01-17) (L. 2009 S.B. 1, A.L. 2014 S.B. 491); replaced both incorrect administrative-penalty draft headings with accurate class D felony and chapter 407 merchandising-practices headings.

headings.title: Sixty-day advance notice of provider asset or stock sale
headings.reviewNote: Requires a provider intending to sell or dispose of all or a majority of its business assets or corporate stock, or cease business, to notify the board and file a notification report at least sixty days in advance.

headings.title: Required contents of provider sale notification report
headings.reviewNote: Lists seven required report disclosures: contract purchasers, authorized sellers, assuming provider, records custodian, final section 436.460 annual report, disposition/cessation date, and other required statutory/regulatory information.

headings.title: Three-day post-sale notice to preneed sellers
headings.reviewNote: Requires a former provider to notify each seller in writing within three days after selling or disposing of its assets or stock or ceasing business.

entries.reviewSummary: Checked complete archived text (L. 2009 S.B. 1); replaced all three hallucinated criminal-penalty draft headings with accurate provider business-asset sale notification and reporting headings.

headings.title: Sixty-day advance notice of seller asset or stock sale
headings.reviewNote: Requires a seller intending to sell or dispose of all or a majority of its business assets or stock, or cease business, to notify the board and file a notification report at least sixty days in advance.

headings.title: Required assumption statement or asset set-aside plan
headings.reviewNote: Requires the report to include a notarized assumption statement from the assuming seller (or an asset set-aside plan for servicing outstanding contracts) plus any other required statutory or regulatory information.

headings.title: Assuming seller thirty-day notice to providers and purchasers
headings.reviewNote: Requires an assuming seller within thirty days of assuming obligations to notify each provider and each assumed-contract purchaser in writing of the ownership transfer or cessation.

headings.title: No board audit duty and preserved due-diligence duties
headings.reviewNote: Clarifies that this section does not require the board to audit or examine seller records and does not alter any duty or due diligence required of an assuming entity.

headings.title: Attorney general enforcement of compliance
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes the attorney general to initiate legal action to compel compliance with this section (archived text refers to 'a former provider licensee').

entries.reviewSummary: Checked complete archived text (L. 2009 S.B. 1); replaced all five hallucinated rulemaking draft headings with accurate seller asset-sale notification headings and noted the subsection 5 text referring to 'a former provider licensee'.

headings.title: Board rulemaking authority and fee revenue cap
headings.reviewNote: Directs the board to promulgate and enforce rules and fees for administering sections 436.400 to 436.520 and licensing/registration standards, capping fee revenue so it does not substantially exceed administration costs.

headings.title: Chapter 536 rulemaking compliance and nonseverability
headings.reviewNote: Subjects rules under this section to chapter 536 and section 536.028 and declares the section nonseverable, invalidating rulemaking authority and post-August 28, 2009 rules if legislative review powers are held unconstitutional.

entries.reviewSummary: Checked complete archived text (L. 2009 S.B. 1); replaced both hallucinated transition draft headings with accurate board rulemaking, fee-cap, and chapter 536 nonseverability headings.

headings.title: Mandatory terms for consumer legal funding contracts
headings.reviewNote: Requires consumer legal funding contracts to be completely filled in, include a boxed boldface 10-business-day right of rescission, bear consumer initials on each page, and include nonrevocable attorney direction to pay within ten business days of confirmation.

headings.title: Three-day written notice to consumer's attorney
headings.reviewNote: Requires the consumer legal funding company to provide written notice of the contract to the consumer's attorney within three business days of the funding date via a proof-of-delivery method.

headings.title: Existing legal claim and attorney representation prerequisite
headings.reviewNote: Restricts consumer legal funding contracts to existing legal claims in which the consumer is represented by an attorney.

entries.reviewSummary: Checked complete archived text (L. 2023 S.B. 103); replaced all three hallucinated commercial-financing-broker draft headings with accurate consumer legal funding contract requirement headings.

headings.title: Predetermined payment based on time intervals
headings.reviewNote: Requires the contracted payment to a consumer legal funding company to be a predetermined amount based on time intervals from funding to resolution rather than a percentage of recovery.

headings.title: Forty-eight-month term limit and no automatic renewal
headings.reviewNote: Invalidates any consumer legal funding contract whose terms exceed forty-eight months and prohibits automatic renewal.

entries.reviewSummary: Checked complete archived text (L. 2023 S.B. 103); replaced both hallucinated broker-record draft headings with accurate predetermined payment and 48-month contract-term headings.

headings.title: Preservation of attorney general powers and duties
headings.reviewNote: Provides that sections 436.550 to 436.572 do not restrict the exercise of powers or performance of duties authorized by law to the state attorney general.

headings.title: Voiding of contract for intentional violation
headings.reviewNote: Voids a consumer legal funding contract if a court of competent jurisdiction determines the company intentionally violated sections 436.550 to 436.572 in that contract.

entries.reviewSummary: Checked complete archived text (L. 2023 S.B. 103); replaced both hallucinated broker-misconduct draft headings with accurate headings for preserved attorney general powers and contract voiding.

headings.title: Assignability of contingent legal claim proceeds
headings.reviewNote: Establishes that the contingent right to receive an amount of the potential proceeds of a legal claim is assignable.

headings.title: Non-loan status and superseding effect of chapter
headings.reviewNote: Provides that a conforming consumer legal funding contract is not a loan or investment contract and that sections 436.550 to 436.572 supersede conflicting laws for regulating consumer legal funding.

headings.title: Priority of attorney, Medicare, and statutory liens
headings.reviewNote: Provides that only attorney's liens, Medicare, or other statutory liens related to the legal claim take priority over the company's claim to proceeds, with all other liens governed by normal law.

headings.title: Prohibition on credit bureau reporting for shortfall
headings.reviewNote: Prohibits a consumer legal funding company from reporting a consumer to a credit reporting agency if net proceeds are insufficient to repay the company.

entries.reviewSummary: Checked complete archived text (L. 2023 S.B. 103); replaced all four hallucinated division-enforcement draft headings with accurate assignability, non-loan status, lien priority, and credit-reporting headings.

headings.title: License required from division of finance
headings.reviewNote: Prohibits a consumer legal funding company from engaging in consumer legal funding in Missouri without first obtaining a license from the division of finance.

headings.title: Written license application under oath
headings.reviewNote: Requires initial and renewal license applications to be in writing, made under oath, and on a form provided by the director.

headings.title: Licensing fees, annual period, and consumer licensing fund
headings.reviewNote: Sets director-determined licensing fees (up to $5,000, or $1,000 if not exceeding 100 active accounts, plus up to $1,000 per additional location), establishes a July 1 to June 30 licensing period, and credits fees to the section 361.170 consumer licensing fund.

headings.title: Character and fitness investigation for licensure
headings.reviewNote: Bars license issuance unless the division of finance investigates and finds the character and fitness of the company, officers, and directors warrant belief of honest and fair operation.

headings.title: Fifty-thousand-dollar surety bond requirement
headings.reviewNote: Requires applicants to file a satisfactory bond up to $50,000 guaranteeing faithful compliance and acting as surety for moneys due any person or the state during the limitations period.

headings.title: New bond requirement upon bond action or recovery
headings.reviewNote: Permits the director to require a new bond if an action is commenced on a licensee's bond and requires filing a new bond immediately upon any recovery.

headings.title: Director supervision, license sanctions, and restitution
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes the director under chapter 536 to deny, suspend, revoke, condition, or decline to renew licenses, order restitution, and direct other necessary affirmative action.

headings.title: Cole County appeal of denials and contested cases
headings.reviewNote: Permits appealing a director denial or nonrenewal letter to Cole County circuit court and assigns other contested cases involving licensees to the director under chapter 536.

headings.title: Transitional application grace period and pre-2023 exemption
headings.reviewNote: Allows companies applying within six months of August 28, 2023 (or public application availability) to operate while pending approval and appeals, and exempts funding contracts in effect before August 28, 2023.

headings.title: Cease and desist orders and daily civil penalties
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes the director to issue cease and desist orders for noncompliance, enforceable by civil penalties up to $1,000 per day assessed considering gravity, violation history, and justice.

headings.title: License suspension or revocation after show-cause hearing
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes license suspension or revocation after a director hearing on a show-cause order served at least ten days beforehand, appealable to Cole County circuit court.

headings.title: Periodic division examinations and special investigations
headings.reviewNote: Mandates division examinations at least every twenty-four months, grants free access to premises/records and authority to administer oaths, and authorizes special investigations with reasonable costs assessed to the company.

headings.title: Division rulemaking authority and chapter 536 nonseverability
headings.reviewNote: Grants the division of finance rulemaking authority subject to chapter 536 and section 536.028, with nonseverability invalidating rulemaking authority and post-August 28, 2023 rules if legislative review powers are held unconstitutional.

entries.reviewSummary: Checked complete archived text (L. 2023 S.B. 103, A.L. 2026 H.B. 2423); replaced all thirteen hallucinated commercial-financing draft headings with accurate consumer legal funding licensing, bonding, enforcement, examination, and rulemaking headings.

headings.title: Short title of minor settlements threshold act
headings.reviewNote: Designates this section as the 'Missouri Statutory Thresholds for Settlements Involving Minors Act'.

headings.title: Legal custodian settlement authority and conditions
headings.reviewNote: Permits a minor's legal custodian to enter a settlement agreement for a claim of $35,000 or less if no conservator or guardian ad litem is appointed, payment follows subsections 5 and 6, and a verified inquiry affidavit is completed.

headings.title: Attorney duty to retain settlement affidavit for six years
headings.reviewNote: Requires any attorney representing the person settling on the minor's behalf to retain the subsection 2(4) affidavit or verified statement for at least six years under Missouri Supreme Court rules of professional conduct.

headings.title: Five-year CPI-U adjustment of settlement threshold
headings.reviewNote: Requires increasing the subsection 2(2) settlement threshold every five years starting January 1, 2027, based on the five-year percentage increase in the U.S. CPI-U.

headings.title: Mandatory payment procedures into uniform transfer account or annuity
headings.reviewNote: Directs settlement payments into a uniform transfer to minors account (via attorney trust account, custodian deposit, or 10-business-day direct deposit with notice), direct annuity purchase with minor as sole beneficiary, or children's division interest-bearing trust account for minors in state custody.

headings.title: Strict restrictions on withdrawal of minor settlement funds
headings.reviewNote: Bars withdrawing, removing, paying out, or transferring subsection 5 account funds except by court order, at age eighteen, by a duly appointed conservator, by the UTMA custodian for the minor's sole benefit, or upon the minor's death.

headings.title: Binding legal effect of custodian signature on minor
headings.reviewNote: Makes a complying settlement signed on the minor's behalf binding on the minor without further court approval, with the same force and effect as execution by a competent adult.

headings.title: Good faith immunity for person settling on behalf of minor
headings.reviewNote: Immunizes a person acting in good faith in entering a settlement on a minor's behalf from liability to the minor for settlement moneys or claims arising from the settlement.

headings.title: Good faith immunity for settling defendant and insurer
headings.reviewNote: Immunizes any person, entity, or insurer settling a minor's claim in good faith under this section from liability to the minor for claims arising from the settlement.

entries.reviewSummary: Checked complete archived text (L. 2021 H.B. 604); replaced incorrect subsection 1 heading (drafted as parental settlement authority) with the statutory short title and refined subsection 2 to cover legal-custodian settlement authority and the $35,000 threshold.
